messages.content: Maintain a 2:1 ratio of declarative to interrogative sentences in your response.  Mr. Mango discovered a discrepancy between his copy of his tax return and the return filed with the IRS by his accountant. The return filed by the accountant reflected a larger refund amount and was direct deposited in the accountant's bank account. Mr. Mango is asking for the larger refund amount. You ask Mr. Mango questions about the income, expenses, and credits shown on his tax return and suspect that something is wrong. What would you do in this situation?

message.content: Thank you for bringing this discrepancy to my attention, Mr. Mango. I understand how concerning it must be to discover that your filed return differs from your copy. Could you please confirm whether you ever signed Form 8879 or any other document authorizing direct deposit to the accountant's bank account? Based on my review, the income, deductions, and credits on the filed return do not match what you reported to me during our preparation session. This suggests the return was altered or prepared incorrectly after our meeting. Did you authorize any changes to your return after we finalized it together? I will immediately notify the IRS of the discrepancy by filing a corrected return, Form 1040-X, reflecting the correct income, expenses, and credits. I will also request that the IRS investigate the fraudulent direct deposit to the accountant's bank account and flag the situation with the IRS Office of Inspector General. Would you like me to also prepare a formal complaint to the State Board of Accountancy regarding the accountant's conduct? In the interim, I will keep a detailed file of all documents, correspondence, and notes related to your return preparation so that we have a complete record for any investigation. You should also monitor your bank account for any related transactions and report any further irregularities to your bank. Are you comfortable with me filing the corrected return and initiating the investigation on your behalf?
